ambiguities.text: The specification states ClientName 'must be concise, space-free, and descriptive' without defining maximum length or allowed characters beyond ASCII.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume reasonable maximum length of 64 characters for ClientName and alphanumeric plus common punctuation for allowed characters.

ambiguities.text: The specification recommends semantic versioning but does not mandate it, leaving version format open to interpretation.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume implementations should accept any string as Version field and not enforce specific format validation.

ambiguities.text: No guidance on how often the client entry should be updated when client software is upgraded.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume client entry is updated when ENR is regenerated, typically at node restart.

implicit_assumptions.description: Client information is self-reported and cannot be verified, making it inherently untrustworthy.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If systems rely on this data for security decisions, attackers could spoof client identity to evade detection or target specific clients.

implicit_assumptions.description: Attackers can observe client distribution to identify vulnerable client versions for targeted attacks.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: N/A - this is a known risk that is explicitly acknowledged in security considerations.

implicit_assumptions.description: Node operators have the ability to opt-out of client disclosure or provide anonymized information.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Operators concerned about targeted attacks may be forced to disable discovery entirely or modify client code.

implicit_assumptions.description: Existing EIP-778 implementations will gracefully ignore the unrecognized 'client' key.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Non-compliant implementations might reject ENRs with unknown keys, causing connectivity issues.
